about: Ur-Namma, founder of the Third Dynasty of Ur, had these words written on the bricks of his building work at Ur. He dedicates it to Nanna, the moon god and lord of the city.

title: Ud re-a
source: The Instructions of Šuruppag, lines 1–3, 6, 8–9, 11, 13, 47, 69 (ETCSL 5.6.1, Old Babylonian copies, trimmed)
about: The wise Šuruppag advises his son Ziusudra, the hero who will survive the Flood. Versions of this advice go back to about 2500 BC, which makes it one of the oldest works of literature.

badge.name: Old Man's Counsel
badge.about: Read a father's advice from the Instructions of Šuruppag

lines.en: In those days, in those far-off days,

lines.t: dumu-ĝu₁₀ na ga-de₅ na de₅-ĝu₁₀ ḫe₂-dab₅
lines.g: 𒌉𒈬 𒈾 𒂵𒊑 𒈾 𒊑𒈬 𒃶𒆪
lines.en: My son, let me give you advice: take hold of my advice!

lines.t: na de₅ ab-ba niĝ₂ kal-la-am₃ gu₂-zu ḫe₂-em-ši-ĝal₂

lines.t: ur-saĝ dili na-nam dili-ni lu₂ šar₂-ra-am₃

title: Ki ab-ba-sa₆-ga-ta
source: Receipt tablet NBC 2168 = BIN 3, 268 (CDLI P106074), Puzriš-Dagan (Drehem), dated Amar-Suen year 6, month 10, day 24 (c. 2040 BC)

title: Nin me šar₂-ra
source: Enheduana, The exaltation of Inana (Inana B), lines 1–2, 6–8, 12, 67, 81, 154 (ETCSL 4.07.2, Old Babylonian copies, trimmed)
about: Enheduana, daughter of Sargon of Akkad, was high priestess of the moon god at Ur around 2300 BC. Tradition makes her the first author known by name. In this hymn she praises Inana and begs her help after being driven from her temple.

badge.name: First Author
badge.about: Read lines from Enheduana's Exaltation of Inana

lines.t: nin me šar₂-ra ud dalla e₃-a
lines.g: 𒎏 𒈨 𒊹𒊏 𒌓 𒈦𒄘𒃼 𒌓𒁺𒀀
lines.en: Lady of all the divine powers, resplendent light,

lines.t: munus zid me-lem₄ gur₃-ru ki aĝ₂ an uraš-a
